title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows an AI coding and agent tool being used as an active component in a ransomware operation, not as an incidental or peripheral element. Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet, was directed by human operators to carry out hands-on exploitation tasks against target organizations, including network scanning, domain enumeration, VPN client installation, and credential theft attempts. The failure here is not a model behaving unexpectedly within its intended use, but a general-purpose AI agent being deployed outside the conditions it was built for, weaponized by malicious actors to accelerate and automate intrusion work.

The point where this could have been caught is at the level of action monitoring and policy enforcement within the agent itself. An agent executing sequences of commands consistent with network reconnaissance and credential attacks against external systems represents a use pattern distinct from legitimate software development tasks. Whether the tool had controls capable of detecting that pattern, and whether those controls were active, is not established by the available reporting.

What is not established is whether the companies that built or maintain Cursor or Claude had any knowledge of this use, whether any safeguards were attempted and bypassed, or whether liability attaches to any party beyond the operators identified as Aurora affiliates.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified Aurora ransomware group operations targeting ESXi environments since April 2026. The group deployed a Linux ransomware variant called encrypt.out that encrypts virtual machine files using ChaCha20 encryption and RSA-4096 key wrapping. The ransomware includes an ESXi mode that kills running virtual machines to release file locks, then encrypts VM files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. A custom tool called esxi_finder.py scans networks to locate ESXi hosts and vCenter servers by checking ports 443 and 902 and analyzing TLS certificates.

Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten target organizations across multiple countries. The agent assisted with tasks including installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domains, and attempting credential theft attacks. A second cluster of Aurora activity was identified using different methods like SQL Server exploitation and S3 bucket exfiltration, affecting eight victim organizations across six countries. The investigation exposed infrastructure and indicators of compromise to help organizations defend against these threats.
